50557912.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant PDE4D by surface plasmon resonance assay
50557912.references_previous: 10. Yu, Q.; Chen, S.; Taylor, A. D.; Homola, J.; Hock, B.; Jiang, S. Sens. Actuators, B 2005, 193, 107. 11. De Lean, A.; Munson, P. J.; Rodbard, D. Am. J. Physiol. 1978, 235, E97.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: By the SPR inhibition assays, we examined YTX, desulfo-YTX, PbTx2 (1, 2, and 3 in Fig. 1), and artificial ladder-shaped polyethers (ALPs 4–6 in Fig. 2) which were previously synthesized in our laboratory.8a–c Biotinylated dsYTX (Scheme 1, see Supplementary data for details) was prepared from YTX by desulfation and conjugation with biotinylated PEG aldehyde, and then immobilized on the surface of a sensor chip via streptavidin. Detection of LSPs was carried out in HBS-EP+ buffer (BiacoreAB) containing 1% DMSO as running and injection media, and PDEII (5 μg/mL) dissolved in HBS-EP+ buffer containing 1% DMSO was passed on the surface of the sensor chip modified with biotinylated dsYTX at a flow rate of 10 μL/min for 2 min. The SPR response increased immediately after injection due to interaction between free PDEII in a sample solution and biotinylated dsYTX immobilized on the surface of sensor chip as shown in Figure 3. Dose-dependent SPR responses were recorded for a series of concentrations of PDEII. After each measurement, the surface of a sensor chip was regenerated by injecting 0.5% SDS, which brought the SPR response back to the original level. In order to obtain high responses in a stable sensorgram, we implemented the inhibition assays at the PDEII concentration of 5 μg/mL. We then incubated various LSPs as analyte in the range of 0–50 μM (or 100 μM in the case of a sample with low affinity). Figure 4 shows the sensorgrams in the presence of various concentrations of YTX, dsYTX and PbTx2. In these assays, the SPR response decreased with increasing concentrations of LSPs in a sample solution. We adopted the increment of the response during 20–40 s after the sample loading for evaluating the inhibition by LSP (Fig. 5) as often used in the inhibition protocol.10 Curve fitting to the experimental data was carried out by using BIAevaluation software (BiacoreAB) with four-parameter logistic equation which was widely adopted to produce dose–response curves (see Supplementary data).11 Figure 5 demonstrates the dose–response curves of the inhibition assays for YTX (A), dsYTX (B), and PbTx2 (C), which led to estimation of 50% inhibitory concentrations (IC50) as shown in Table 1.

PDEII solutions were injected at 0 (gray), 1 (red), 2 (magenta), and 5 (blue) μg/mL in HBS-EP+ containing 1% DMSO. After 120 s, the PDEII solutions was changed to wash buffer.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. SPR sensorgrams of 5 μg/mL PDEII in HBS-EP+ containing 1% DMSO solution with 0 (red), 0.5 (magenta), 2 (blue), and 20 (green) μM of inhibiting LSPs, A, YTX, B, dsYTX, and C, PbTx2, which were injected to biotinylated dsYTX immobilized on the surface of sensor chip via streptavidin.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. Dose–response inhibition curves for 5 μg/mL PDEII by 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, and 50 μM LSPs against biotinylated dsYTX immobilized on the surface of sensor chip via streptavidin. These curves demonstrate on A, YTX; B, dsYTX and C, PbTx2.
original_paragraph.Table 1: Table 1 Half inhibitory concentrations (IC50, μM) of LSPs as analyte against PDEII in inhibition detection assays Assay methods IC50 ± SEM (μM) YTX 1 3.0 ± 1.0 dsYTX 2 1.7 ± 0.2 PbTx2 3 1.8 ± 1.0 4 – 5A – 5B 13.0 ± 2.7 6 9.2 ± 0.9 Salinomycin 7 – SEM was determined from three independent experiments. * IC50 was estimated to be over 100 μM. Experimental details are provided in Supplementary data.
original_paragraph.Results section: In the present study we demonstrated for the first time that the inhibition SPR method is useful for evaluating LSPs–protein interactions, particularly for screening receptor proteins, since it is not necessary to prepare a receptor-immobilized sensor chip. Some of LSPs are known to be responsible for seafood poisoning and need to be monitored carefully. Recently, enzyme-linked immunoassays have been developed for detecting ciguatoxin,9d,12 for which high-affinity antibodies with nanomolar KD values are used. These specific assays to the major causative toxin would partly address the serious problems of ciguatera. On the other hand, LSPs tested in this study showed relatively low affinity to binding proteins. Among those, ALPs 5B, 6 and PbTx2 revealed higher affinity to PDEII but salinomycin or 4 did not. The results suggest that PDEII loosely recognizes the ladder-shaped skeletal structures, and sometimes works better with receptors with strict recognition since a great variety of LSP toxins are often involved in seafood poisoning, particularly in the case of shellfish poisoning. Among other SPR-based methods reported so far,7,13 the present inhibition assays may provide a practical way for estimating LSP toxins in seafood and marine organisms.
original_paragraph.Figure 6 caption: Figure 6. (A) SPR sensorgrams of direct method for YTX against PDEII. YTX was injected in the range from 0 to 50 μM. Color in trace corresponds to concentration of YTX: 0 (gray), 10 (red), 20 (magenta), 30 (blue), 40 (light blue), and 50 (light green) μM in HBS-EP+ containing 1% DMSO solution. (B) Concentration-dependent SPR responses and a theoretical curve for KD of 2.2 μM.
